name: Lakhamandal Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in the Jaunsar-Bawar hills above the Yamuna, whose surviving shikhara is dated to the 12th–13th century while brick remains on the site go back several centuries earlier. A sixth-century inscription found here records that a princess named Ishwara of Singhpura raised a shrine in memory of her husband Chandragupta, and Archaeological Survey excavations have recovered a large quantity of sculpture around it.
story: Local tradition ties the site to the Mahabharata, holding that this is where Duryodhana built the lac house in which he meant to burn the Pandavas alive.

name: Muringamangalam Sreemahadevar Temple
significance: The largest Shiva temple in Pathanamthitta district, with an east-facing Mahadeva sanctum and subsidiary shrines to Ganapathi, Ayyappa, the nagas and Krishna. It was historically held by the Pandalam royal family.

name: Kailasanathar Temple, Nedungudi
deity: Shiva as Kailasanathar (also Kasinathar), with the goddess Prasannanayaki
significance: A Shiva temple on the Karaikkudi–Aranthangi road holding two lingas, whose goddess shrine to Prasannanayaki is dated to the 13th century. The complex has the usual sequence of garbhagriha, artha mandapa and maha mandapa.
story: Two asura brothers, Perunjeevi and Siranjeevi, were told by Vishnu to worship Shiva together here; the deity is also called Padikkasunathar after a tale of abhisheka milk poured here appearing on the steps at Kashi.

name: Lakshmi Narayan Temple, Bhopal
significance: A hilltop Birla temple in Bhopal whose foundation stone was laid in 1960 by Madhya Pradesh chief minister Kailashnath Katju and which was inaugurated in 1964 by Dwarka Prasad Mishra. Besides the Lakshmi Narayan sanctum it houses images of Shiva, Jagdamba and Hanuman.

name: Vedapureeswarar Temple, Thiruverkadu
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of about 1.5 acres with two gopurams, praised in the 7th-century Tevaram hymns; the original complex is held to predate that century and is attributed to the Cholas. The present structure was rebuilt in 1973 and the temple is run by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.
story: Sage Agastya, kept from seeing Shiva's wedding at Kailasa by the crowd, prayed here and was granted the sight of Shiva and Parvati in their wedding dress.

name: Sikri Mata Temple
deity: Sikri Mata, held to be a form of Durga
significance: A goddess temple founded in 1532 by Jalim Giri Baba of the Goswami community, according to Bhaat records. During the 1857 rebellion more than 130 rebels were hanged from an old banyan tree on its grounds; the shrine passed from the founder's descendants to the gram panchayat in 1977 and to the Modinagar municipal body in 2024.
story: Jalim Giri Baba is said to have built the shrine after a darshan of Durga told him to raise it on that spot.

name: Madhya Kailash Temple
significance: A busy Vinayakar temple at the junction of Sardar Patel Road and Rajiv Gandhi Salai in Adyar, with the main deity ringed by shrines to Shiva, Surya, Devi and Vishnu as well as Anjaneya and Swarna Bhairavar.
story: Its best-known image is the Adhyantha Prabhu, half Ganesha and half Hanuman, said to have been made after a temple official saw that combined form in a vision.

name: Nileshwar Muthappan Madappura
deity: Muthappan, worshipped in theyyam form as Vishnu
significance: A madappura in the north Kerala town of Nileshwar dedicated to Muthappan, the folk deity of the Malabar coast whose worship centres on theyyam performance.

name: Nageshvara Temple, Begur
significance: A temple complex on the southern edge of Bengaluru whose two principal shrines were raised under the Western Ganga kings Nitimarga I and Ereyappa Nitimarga II, with later additions in Chola, Hoysala and Vijayanagara idiom. An Old Kannada inscription of about 890 found here carries the earliest known mention of the name Bengaluru.
story: Ravana is said to have worshipped Nageshvara here on his way back to Lanka after losing the atma linga at Gokarna.

name: Mudikondan Kothandaramar Temple
deity: Vishnu as Kothandaramar (Rama), with Yogasayana Perumal and Ranganathar
significance: A Vishnu temple in Nannilam taluk held to predate the age of the Alvars, with sanctums for Rama as Kothandaramar, Yogasayana Perumal and Ranganathar.
story: Returning from Lanka, Rama is said to have halted at sage Bharadwaja's hermitage here and shown himself in coronation form before the actual crowning at Ayodhya, which is how the village got the name Mudikondan.

name: Tirttanakiri Sivakozhundeesvarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Shivakozhundhu Easwarar, with Oppila Nayaki
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, the Shiva shrines sung in the Tamil Tevaram canon; this one was praised by the Nayanar Sundarar in the early medieval period.

name: Sri Sri Nilakantheswar Temple
deity: Shiva, as a lingam set in a circular laterite yoni
significance: A west-facing twentieth-century Shiva temple in the Bhimatangi neighbourhood of western Bhubaneswar, built in the Kalinga manner of the older temples of the city.

name: Tholudur Madhurantaka Choleswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in the village of Tholudur in Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu, where the presiding deity is worshipped as Madhurantaka Choleswarar.

name: Kokarneswarar Temple, Thirukokarnam
significance: A rock-cut temple excavated for the Pallava king Mahendravarman I around the middle of the 7th century, with Chola and Pandya additions early in the second millennium. Its goddess Brihadambal was the family deity of the Thondaiman rulers of Pudukkottai, and the shrine is reckoned among the oldest accurately datable stone temples still in worship.

name: Mukteshwar Mahadev Temple
deity: Shiva, as a white marble lingam in a copper yoni
significance: A cave temple on a hilltop above the Ravi about 22 km from Pathankot, on the Shahpur Kandi dam road, holding a marble lingam along with images of Ganesha, Brahma, Vishnu, Hanuman and Parvati. It is among the most visited shrines in the Pathankot area.
story: The name is explained by a tale that Shiva killed a demon here and granted him mukti, and the caves are said to have sheltered the Pandavas during their exile.

name: Brahma Temple, Khajuraho
significance: A small Chandela shrine on the bank of the Khajuraho Sagar, part of the UNESCO World Heritage group, built of granite rather than the sandstone of most Khajuraho temples and so read as transitional between the two materials. Only the sanctum and its sandstone shikhara survive; the temple is misnamed, since worshippers took its four-faced Shiva lingam for an image of the four-faced Brahma.

name: Mylara Lingeshwara Temple
deity: Mylara Lingeshwara, a form of Shiva
significance: The temple of Mylara Lingeshwara, a regional form of Shiva, in Mylara village of Hoovina Hadagali taluk in northern Karnataka.

name: Tapkeshwar Temple
deity: Shiva, as a natural cave shivalinga
significance: A cave shrine on the bank of the Tons at Dehradun, built over a natural shivalinga onto which water drips continuously from the rock above — the feature that gives the temple its name.
story: The cave is linked to Dronacharya: when his wife could not nurse their son Ashwatthama and the family could not afford milk, the boy prayed to Shiva, who fed him with milk dripping from the lingam.

name: Narasingam Yoga Narasimha Perumal Temple
significance: A cave temple cut into the Yanaimalai hill 8 km from Madurai, begun in 770 CE by Maran Kari, minister to the Pandya king, and finished by his brother Maran Eyinan; the six-foot Yoga Narasimha is carved from the living rock. Inscriptions record later endowments by Srivallabha Pandya and Sundara Pandya, and there is a separate stone shrine for the goddess Narasingavalli.
story: The Sthala Purana says sage Romasa did penance here for a child and asked to see the Narasimha avatar; the form proved so fierce that Prahlada and Mahalakshmi had to calm it, leaving the seated Yoga Narasimha worshipped today.

name: Nagesvara Temple, Bhubaneswar
deity: Shiva, as a lingam in the garbhagriha
significance: A Shiva temple on the western bank of the Lingaraja west canal in Bhubaneswar, built of ochreous sandstone carved in the Kalinga manner. Local tradition credits it to the Kesari rulers; it remains in worship and in generally sound condition apart from surface decay.

name: Dhenupureeswarar Temple, Madambakkam
significance: A Chola temple of the reign of Parantaka Chola II, later consolidated in stone under Kulothunga Chola I, notable for its apsidal gajaprishta vimana shaped like an elephant's back. It had fallen into ruin before being rediscovered and restored by devotees on the guidance of the Kanchi acharya Maha Periyava, and is now a nationally protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India.
story: Sage Kapila, punished for worshipping a Shiva lingam with his left hand, was reborn as a cow; the cow poured its milk over a buried lingam here, and when it was found Shiva granted the sage release.

name: Mondaicaud Amman Temple
significance: A goddess temple near Colachel on the Kanyakumari coast, so heavily attended by women pilgrims that it is called the women's Sabarimala; its Maasi Kodai festival is the chief annual event. It is noticed in nineteenth-century writing including the Aithiga Mala of 1889 and in district gazetteers.

name: Therazhundur Vedapureeswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam on the Kaveri, sung by the Nayanar Tirugnanasambandar and known in older texts as Thirunedungalam. The Archaeological Survey has recorded Tamil inscriptions on its door jambs dated to the 34th and 44th regnal years of Kulottunga Chola I.

name: Kandaswami Temple, George Town
deity: Murugan as Kandhaswami, with Deivanai and Valli
significance: Known as Kandhakottam, this Murugan temple near Parry's Corner was founded in the 1670s by Maari Chettiar around an image brought from a tank near Thiruporur, and rebuilt in stone in the early 1800s. It covers about eight acres, is administered by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department, and is remembered as a place of worship of the saint Ramalinga Swamigal.

name: Navalinga Temple, Kukkanur
significance: A cluster of nine shrines with shikharas raised in the ninth century under the Rashtrakuta kings Amoghavarsha I or Krishna II, built in poor sandstone but richly carved and now much weathered. Old Kannada inscriptions on the site, dated between 1005 and 1186, record grants to shrines of several goddesses and to Mallikarjuna; lintels over the entrances carry Gajalakshmi.

name: Sri Dakshinamukha Nandi Tirtha Kalyani Kshetra
deity: Shiva, as a shivalinga fed by the Nandi's spout
significance: A sunken temple on 2nd Temple Street in Malleswaram, built as a pillared corridor around a stepped tank, in which water runs constantly from the mouth of an unusual south-facing Nandi onto the lingam below. Buried for centuries, it was uncovered in 1997 when residents opposed building work on the plot and the ground was excavated.
story: The spring feeding the tank is held to be the sacred source of the river Vrishabhavati.

name: Thiruthuraipoondi Piravi Marundeeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Piravi Marundeeswarar, also worshipped as Gajasamharamurthy
significance: A Shiva temple in Tiruvarur district counted among the Tamil nakshatra temples, this one being the shrine of those born under the Ashvini birth star.

name: Ranganathaswamy Temple, Karamadai
deity: Vishnu as Ranganathaswamy, with Ranganayaki Thayar and Bettadamman
significance: A Vishnu temple 23 km from Coimbatore on the Mettupalayam road, first built under the Cholas and enlarged by Tirumalai Nayakar in the seventeenth century and by Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar in the 1940s; its northern tower dates to 1944 and the seven-tiered eastern rajagopuram was finished in 2013. It is counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams, follows the Tenkalai tradition, and is run by the state endowments department.
story: A herdsman is said to have found the deity's face beneath an anthill after his cow bled into it.

name: Gauthameswarar Temple, Kumbakonam
deity: Shiva as Gauthameswarar, with Soundara Nayaki
significance: A Shiva temple on the eastern bank of the Mahamaham tank at Kumbakonam, one of the twelve Shiva shrines tied to the Mahamaham festival held there every twelve years. Its most recent kumbabhishekam was performed in September 2015.
story: A thread from the primordial kumba is said to have fallen here and taken the form of a linga, and sage Gowthama worshipped it to expiate the killing of a cow.

name: Veemeeswarar Temple, Serapanancheri
significance: A Chola temple near Padappai on the Tambaram–Walajabad road whose earliest inscription belongs to Kulothunga Chola III, placing it around 1180. It is unusual for its very large lingam and for having two Nandis, and was once ringed by the Agni, Brahma and Vishnu theerthams, now dry.
story: Surya is said to come here regularly to worship Shiva, and the deity is held to govern all twenty-seven nakshatras.

name: Sree Madiyan Koolom Temple
deity: Kshetrapalan, with Kalarathri Amma (Bhadrakali) and Nadayil Bhagavathi
significance: One of the oldest temples of north Kerala and the seat of the Allada Swaroopam, dedicated to Kshetrapalan alongside the goddess Kalarathri. It admitted worshippers of the lower castes even before the Temple Entry Proclamation.
story: Kshetrapalakan is said to have come to earth at Mahadeva's command to take the Allada country, but was so taken by the smell of appam being made for Nadayil Bhagavathi that he sat down and stayed — his followers calling him Thampuran Madiya, the lazy lord, from which the name Madiyan comes.

name: Ambamata Temple
significance: A goddess temple at Udaipur completed in Vikram Samvat 1721, corresponding to 1664, by Maharana Raj Singh of Mewar, on the spot where an image of the goddess was dug out of the ground.
story: Raj Singh, suffering from an eye ailment no physician could cure, was preparing to travel to the Ambika Mata shrine in the Arbuda hills when the goddess told him in a dream that she would come to Mewar instead; the image was unearthed where she indicated and his sight was restored.

name: Choleesvarar Temple, Mulanur
significance: A Shiva temple at Mulanur counted among the Vaippu Sthalams named in the hymns of the Nayanar Sundarar, with subsidiary shrines to Vinayaka, Subramanya with Valli and Deivanai, Surya, Bhairava and Nataraja.

name: Elumur Ardhanareeswarar Temple
significance: A Vaippu Sthalam sung by the Nayanar Appar and therefore held to have existed by the seventh century; the name Elumur, 'place of seven', is explained by seven sages said to have worshipped Shiva here. After the temple fell into ruin the lingam and other images were found buried in the silt of a tank, reinstalled first under a thatched roof and later in a permanent shrine, which is why the deity is also called Jalakandeswarar.

name: Mannar Thrikkuratti Mahadeva Temple
deity: Shiva, with a separate srikovil for Krishna
significance: One of the 108 famous Shiva temples of Kerala, standing on the bank of the Pampa at Mannar, with a Shiva sanctum and a separate shrine for Krishna.
story: Folklore credits Parashurama with installing the image, and holds that the temple's enormous compound wall was raised in a single night by a troupe of Shiva's bhutas.

name: Cochin Thirumala Devaswom
deity: Vishnu as Venkatachalapathi, with Sreedevi and Bhoodevi
significance: The principal temple of the Gowda Saraswat Brahmins of Cochin, consecrated in 1599 by Swami Sudhindra Thirtha for a Venkateshwara image brought from Goa by families fleeing Portuguese persecution. The Portuguese destroyed it in 1662 and it was rebuilt the following year under Dutch rule; after further trouble in 1791 the image was kept at Alappuzha until it was brought back in 1853.
story: The image is held to be swayambhu, said to have been shaped by Vishvakarma himself through a sculptor working for the Vijayanagara king Saluva Narasimha Deva Raya.

name: Vanmeekanathar Temple, Tiruvetriyur
significance: A Shiva temple in Sivagangai district counted among the Vaippu Sthalams sung by the Nayanars Sambandar and Sundarar; locally it is known after the goddess as the Bagampiriyal temple.

name: Karapuranathar Temple
significance: A ninth-century Shiva temple near the west bank of the Thirumanimutharu at Uthamacholapuram, its name compounded from karai (riverbank), puram (place) and nathar (lord). Local historical tradition links the village to the Sangam-age story of Vel Pari, the poet Kapilar and the marriage of Pari's daughters.
story: A devotee named Karadhushan is said to have thrown himself into fire to prove his devotion; Shiva put the flames out, and is worshipped here as Karapuranathar in memory of it.

name: Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple
significance: A Shiva temple of the Chola period in Santharavuru, Chinnaganjam mandal, coastal Andhra Pradesh. Its temple authorities claim a bell that rings out 108 times from a single strike, a property they say is matched only by one bell at Varanasi.

name: Mavelikara Maruthakshi Devi Temple
builtDisplay: records go back at least 60 years
significance: A goddess temple near Mavelikkara railway station in Alappuzha district, dedicated to Maruthakshi Devi with Shiva worshipped as Appuppan, and administered by the Maruthakshi Devaswam.

name: Laloor Bhagavathy Temple
significance: One of the 108 Durga temples of Kerala traditionally ascribed to Parashurama, now under the Cochin Devaswom Board. Its goddess takes part in the Thrissur Pooram, arriving with nine elephants to pay respects at the Vadakkunnathan temple, and the place name is explained as a worn form of yagoor, from the yagas once performed there.
story: A mantra inscribed within the temple is said to be the one the gopis used when they worshipped the goddess to gain Krishna as their husband.

name: Shri Vaijnath Temple
significance: Reckoned the fifth of the twelve jyotirlingas of Shiva, this Hemadpanthi temple at Parli in Beed district stands some 75–80 feet high with a brass-plated eastern doorway, and was renovated in 1706 under Ahilyabai Holkar. It draws its largest crowds at Mahashivratri, and male devotees perform the abhisheka bare above the waist.
